en: When we watch a film or a play, we know that the actors probably learned their lines from a script,
zh: 一首曲子的樂譜類似劇本簡單來說

en: which essentially tells them what to say and when to say it.
zh: 簡單來說樂譜告訴音樂家要彈奏什麼還有彈奏的時間點

en: A piece of written music operates on exactly the same principle.
zh: 雖然每個音樂家的風格不同

en: In a very basic sense, it tells a performer what to play and when to play it.
zh: 比如說，貝多芬和小賈斯汀但兩位音樂家

en: Aesthetically speaking, there's a world of difference between, say, Beethoven and Justin Bieber, but both artists have used
zh: 都用了同樣的基本單位創造音樂: 音符雖然最後的曲子聽起來很複雜但音符的基礎邏輯

en: the same building blocks to create their music: notes.
zh: 其實是簡單易懂的讓我們一起了解樂譜最基本的要素

en: And although the end result can sound quite complicated, the logic behind musical notes is actually pretty straightforward.
zh: 樂譜最基本的要素還有如何做曲曲子是寫在五條平行線上的

notes.example: Actually, we're just looking around for now.

en: Let's take a look at the foundational elements to music notation and how they interact to create a work of art.
zh: 曲子是寫在五條平行線上的五條線橫跨整個頁面也就是五線譜五線譜分兩個軸向

en: Music is written on five parallel lines that go across the page.
zh: 上跟下左跟右

notes.zh: run across someone：偶然遇見某人
notes.example: I ran across an old friend at the bookstore.

en: These five lines are called a staff, and a staff operates on two axes: up and down and left to right.
zh: 上下軸告訴音樂家樂譜的音調或是音符左右軸告訴音樂家音樂的節奏韻律

en: The up-and-down axis tells the performer the pitch of the note or what note to play, and the left-to-right axis
zh: 還有彈奏的時間點首先來看音調用鋼琴來做解釋吧不過鋼琴樂譜的原理

en: tells the performer the rhythm of the note or when to play it.
zh: 不過鋼琴樂譜的原理也可以類推到別的樂器上

en: Let's start with pitch.
zh: 傳統西方音樂裡的音調

en: To help us out, we're going to use a piano, but this system works for pretty much any instrument you can think of.
zh: 音調是用七個英文字母命名 A B C D E

en: In the Western music tradition, pitches are named after the first seven letters of the alphabet, A, B, C, D, E, F, and G.
zh: F 還有G 同樣模式不斷重複 A B C D E F G A B C D E F G 以此類推

en: After that, the cycle repeats itself: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and so on.
zh: 但音調的名字是怎麼來的? 舉例來說，如果你彈F 再彈另一個F 只是高低音不同

en: But how do these pitches get their names?
zh: 其實聽起來差不多

en: Well, for example, if you played an F and then played another F higher or lower on the piano,
zh: 跟B相比就不同了再回到五線譜每條線，還有線與線間的空格

en: you'd notice that they sound pretty similar compared to, say, a B.
zh: 都代表一個音調如果在線上畫上一個音符

en: Going back to the staff, every line and every space between two lines represents a separate pitch.
zh: 或在線與線之間譜上音符演奏者就知道要彈什麼音調五線譜上音符越高

en: If we put a note on one of these lines or one of these spaces, we're telling a performer to play that pitch.
zh: 表示音調越高但音樂有數之不盡的音調不只限於九條線與間的音調

en: The higher up on the staff a note is placed, the higher the pitch.
zh: 不只限於九條線與間的音調以演奏式鋼琴為例可以彈奏８８個音調

en: But there are obviously many, many more pitches than the nine that these lines and spaces gives us.
zh: 可以彈奏８８個音調怎麼把８８個音調塞進五線譜呢? 這就要用譜號來表示

en: A grand piano, for example, can play 88 separate notes.
zh: 這就要用譜號來表示譜號是個怪異的圖形寫在五線譜的前端

en: So how do we condense 88 notes onto a single staff?
zh: 寫在五線譜的前端譜號標示某特定音調告訴你線與間的音符

en: We use something called a clef, a weird-looking figure placed at the beginning of the staff, which acts like a reference point,
zh: 告訴你線與間的音符代表的是鍵盤上哪個音要彈奏五線譜上沒有的音符可以偷偷在譜上多加短線

en: telling you that a particular line or space corresponds to a specific note on your instrument.
zh: 可以偷偷在譜上多加短線也就是加線然後再譜上音符

en: If we want to play notes that aren't on the staff, we kind of cheat and draw extra little lines called ledger lines
zh: 但如果要畫很多加線樂譜會讓人眼花撩亂這時就要變換譜號

en: and place the notes on them.
zh: 演奏者要知道彈奏的時間點

en: If we have to draw so many ledger lines that it gets confusing, then we need to change to a different clef.
zh: 演奏者要知道彈奏的時間點會看兩個地方拍子還有節奏一首曲子的拍子

en: As for telling a performer when to play the notes, two main elements control this: the beat and the rhythm.
zh: 有點單調無聊聽起來像這樣

notes.zh: keep control over...：掌控某人或某事
notes.example: Staying calm helps you keep control over the conversation.

en: The beat of a piece of music is, by itself, kind of boring.
zh: 並沒有什麼變化就這麼周而復始的下去

en: It sounds like this. (Ticking) Notice that it doesn't change, it just plugs along quite happily.
zh: 可以放慢也可以加快隨便你怎麼變化拍子就像時鐘的秒針

en: It can go slow or fast or whatever you like, really.
zh: 將一分鐘分為６０秒每一秒長度都一樣

en: The point is that just like the second hand on a clock divides one minute into sixty seconds,
zh: 拍子將一首曲子分成很多個小段落每一段長度相同

notes.zh: just need a second：請稍等我們一下
notes.example: Sorry, we just need a second to check the menu.

en: with each second just as long as every other second, the beat divides a piece of music
zh: 就是拍子拍子抓準後接下來是節奏

notes.zh: just need a second：請稍等我們一下
notes.example: Sorry, we just need a second to check the menu.

en: into little fragments of time that are all the same length: beats.
zh: 音樂是從節奏開始的這是四分音符

en: With a steady beat as a foundation, we can add rhythm to our pitches, and that's when music really starts to happen.
zh: 節奏最基本單位等於一拍二分音符是兩拍

en: This is a quarter note.
zh: 全音符是四拍

en: It's the most basic unit of rhythm, and it's worth one beat.
zh: 這幾個小蝌蚪是八分音符每個音符是半拍

en: This is a half note, and it's worth two beats.
zh: 每個音符是半拍太棒了！但他們代表什麼啊？

en: This whole note here is worth four beats, and these little guys are eighth notes, worth half a beat each.
zh: 你應該有注意到五線譜上有幾條小線將樂譜分成幾個小段落

en: "Great," you say, "what does that mean?"
zh: 這是小節線

en: You might have noticed that across the length of a staff, there are little lines dividing it into small sections.
zh: 每個段落是一個小節樂譜一開始在譜號後

notes.zh: run across someone：偶然遇見某人
notes.example: I ran across an old friend at the bookstore.

en: These are bar lines and we refer to each section as a bar.
zh: 會有個拍號告訴演奏者一小節有幾拍

en: At the beginning of a piece of music, just after the clef, is something called the time signature,
zh: 這個拍號表示一小節有兩拍這是三拍四拍以此類推

en: which tells a performer how many beats are in each bar.
zh: 以此類推下面的數字告訴我們

en: This says there are two beats in each bar, this says there are three, this one four, and so on.
zh: 要用什麼音符當作一拍一是全音符二是二分音符

en: The bottom number tells us what kind of note is to be used as the basic unit for the beat.
zh: 四是四分音符八是八分音符以此類推樂譜上的拍號

en: One corresponds to a whole note, two to a half note, four to a quarter note, and eight to an eighth note, and so on.
zh: 樂譜上的拍號告訴演奏者一小節有四拍一二三四一二三四

en: So this time signature here tells us that there are four quarter notes in each bar, one, two, three, four; one, two, three, four,
zh: 以此類推但就像之前說的如果只注意拍子會很無趣可以把幾個四分音符換成別的節奏

en: and so on. But like I said before, if we just stick to the beat, it gets kind of boring,
zh: 換成別的節奏注意，雖然音符的數目變了每個小節不一樣但總拍數維持不變

en: so we'll replace some quarter notes with different rhythms.
zh: 但總拍數維持不變

en: Notice that even though the number of notes in each bar has changed, the total number of beats in each bar hasn't.
zh: 這首曲子聽起來如何還可以，但有些單調

en: So, what does our musical creation sound like?
zh: 加入另一個樂器呢配上不同音調與節奏

en: Eh, sounds okay, but maybe a bit thin, right?
zh: 聽起來更像音樂了讀譜是須要練習的

en: Let's add another instrument with its own pitch and rhythm.
zh: 才能一邊讀譜一邊彈奏音樂

en: Now it's sounding like music.
zh: 但只要花點時間跟耐心

en: Sure, it takes some practice to get used to reading it quickly and playing what we see on our instrument,
zh: 或者小賈斯汀

notes.zh: （錄音或拍片）每一次錄製（between takes：錄製空檔）
notes.example: The band kept improvising between takes.

en: but, with a bit of time and patience, you could be the next Beethoven or Justin Bieber.
zh: （對照上方英文字幕跟讀）
